chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is half the dower, if something was obligated for her; and if it was not obligated for her, then let him provide for her with provision in the manner that he would provide for similar women.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Or he should relinquish in whose hand is the marriage tie.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is the father, or the brother, and the man who has been bequeathed to it, and the man whose instructions are allowed in the wealth of the woman, so he buys for her and sells for her. So when he excuses, it is allowed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dower and provision for a woman divorced before consummation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the financial entitlements of a woman divorced before consummation, distinguishing between cases where a specific dower was agreed upon versus those requiring discretionary provision (muta'). It further elucidates the Quranic phrase 'in whose hand is the marriage tie' to include not only the husband but also the father, brother, or guardian who holds authority over her affairs, reflecting the Shia understanding of marital guardianship.
